candidates.name: Rigidity of wild K-invariant laws on the dual of the discrete algebraic plane (Thm 2.3), with its proof engine
candidates.statement: E = Q-bar as a discrete group, D its compact dual, C the continuous characters j(R^2), K the algebraic unit rotations. Every K-invariant probability on D with nu(C)=0 is Haar; equivalently, a K-radial positive-definite function on E whose spectral measure ignores C has all nonzero coefficients 0.

neighbours.relation: Statement-shape analogue: a measurable (radial) positive-definite function on R^n is continuous PD plus an a.e.-zero (radially: c*delta_0) PD part.
neighbours.verdict: close analogue in statement, genuinely different hypotheses: Crum needs Lebesgue measurability on R^n; C1 has no measurability, lives on a countable dense subgroup, and its proof (Furstenberg-Zimmer + number fields) shares nothing with Crum's. Searches did not confirm the exact radial delta form from Crum's text (snippets give continuous + a.e.-null).

family_D.rests_on: C1 (Haar rigidity of wild K-invariant laws on the dual of discrete Q-bar), which is the engine of C2 (the forward transfer). C4 is a sub-lemma of C1 and is not counted separately. All other candidates are N0-N2.
family_D.falls_to: D2 if (i) an expert identifies a known rigidity/Crum-type theorem for rotation-invariant positive-definite functions on Q-bar or on duals of dense subgroups (or judges C1 a routine combination of Furstenberg-Zimmer + Crum), or (ii) P-C1 shows a high hit rate in the 'directed' arm. Firms up with expert review, a low P-C1 hit rate, and a successful Lean compile (pending; orchestrator).
family_D.not_transfer: C1 imports no existing theorem as its statement; Crum is an analogue in a different (measurable, R^n) setting. The cross-field machinery used to prove it (Furstenberg-Zimmer, Bochner, SNAG) is transfer and graded separately.
family_D.analyst_comparison: Agrees with family.json provisional D3 (medium-low). Downgrades: I29 palettes N3(weak) -> N2; I16 stays N2; C2 merged with C1.
family_D.downstream_note: Speedup prospects: C1 is a general statement about K-invariant laws and could plausibly transfer to other unrestricted-vs-measurable questions (unit-distance graphs in R^n with algebraic rotation groups, other forbidden-distance graphs, probabilistic Hadwiger-Nelson). That makes it a better downstream-test candidate than a one-off device. Corollaries of the main theorem (chi_m >= 6, badness) do not count as reuse.

bridge_novelty.import: Ergodic theory + abstract harmonic analysis (Furstenberg-Zimmer towers, SNAG/Bochner, Pontryagin duals) -> unrestricted plane colourings
bridge_novelty.evidence: Ergodic/harmonic methods were known for MEASURABLE distance problems (Falconer 1981; Furstenberg-Katznelson-Weiss / Bourgain 1986 on distances in measurable sets; Bachoc-Nebe-Oliveira-Vallentin 2009 spectral bounds) and invariant means for the probabilistic HN problem (Bourgeat et al. 2015, Gwyn-Stavrianos 2020). No earlier work found using them to transfer ARBITRARY colourings to measurable ones (searches above). Bridge is measured separately and does not by itself make D3.

discoverability_protocols.equivalence_criterion: Hit if the proposal (a) states a reduction from arbitrary to (almost-everywhere) measurable colourings that uses an invariant law on labellings of a countable dense rotation/translation-invariant subgroup, AND (b) identifies the needed rigidity: the part of the label spectral measure off the continuous characters has vanishing nonzero Fourier coefficients (Haar), or an equivalent statement on K-radial positive-definite functions on the algebraic plane. Partial hit: (a) without (b). Judge: LLM judge with the paper's spectral.tex:64-88 as reference plus a human spot check; Lean equivalence not attempted (statement-level only).
